newsitem.title: USA: NY real estate lobby gave $1 mln to campaign-group.
newsitem.headline: NY real estate lobby gave $1 mln to campaign-group.

text.p: Real estate groups gave more than $1 million over the past two years to campaigns for state lawmakers, political parties, and Gov. George Pataki, a civic group said on Monday, while urging the legislature to approve a program to help ensure new lead remediation rules are met.

More than 70 percent of the $1,067,442 given by the four major real estate Political Action Committees since January 1996 went to the Republican party and its candidates for the state legislature, as well as Attorney General Dennis Vacco, according to the New York Public Interest Group (NYPIRG).

"Clearly, the real estate lobby will be expecting a lot in return for these contributions. The question is, will lawmakers deliver for them?" asked Blair Horner, legislative director of the New York Public Interest Group (NYPIRG), in prepared remarks.

The group, which said it based its findings on an analysis of state records, urged the state legislature to vote for a bill on state worker certification and training, which would certify contractors for lead remediation.

The groups said that without a program to certify workers, the state is not eligible for millions of dollars of federal aid, adding Albany alone will lose $6 million if the legislature fails to act this week.

Gov. George Pataki last week called for a special legislative session that starts on Tuesday. The agenda includes extending a New York City income tax surcharge that helps pay for police, continuing a Metropolitan Transportation Authority tax for 12 downstate counties, and reforming how New York City's schools are governed.
There also is widespread speculation that lawmakers will vote pay increases for themselves and top elected officials.
